strongest_candidates.title: Fit the passive spring loop to a Toyota YUBI teleoperation glove

importance.worker: Robot hardware builder preparing the Toyota YUBI finger-driven teleoperation glove
importance.workflow: Official right-glove assembly procedure step11: hook the selected No16 rubber band onto the right finger base, route it onto the holder hook and groove, then confirm smooth finger opening and closing.
importance.consequence: Equips a real robot teleoperation/data-collection interface used with a robot-mounted gripper; this is direct robotics hardware preparation, not an arbitrary household elastic renamed a robot part.
importance.independent_review: Critic independently read Toyota README, exact step11 text/photo and BOM and found the importance/source chain strong.

strongest_candidates.exact_source_quote: Hook rubber band No.16 onto the hook at base of the finger. Use right-finger side for right-hand version and left-finger side for left-hand Version. Hook rubber band onto the hook and groove of HOLDER_Quest_R/L. Confirm that the fingers open and close smoothly.

hardware.product: Toyota YUBI Glove Assy_ver.2, RIGHT-hand version only
hardware.materials: BOM: PLA_BLACK plates/holder/grip, PLA_RED finger parts, POM JZF8-5 bushings, metal fasteners, natural-rubber loop.
hardware.band_identification: BOM row39: RUBBER BAND No16; Kyowa Oband GE011, Japanese Amazon product B000THQ9R2. The source names a real commercially available standard part. No purchase was made.
hardware.band_dimensions: Manufacturer catalog fetch was proxy403. Free loop circumference, cross-section and force–strain curve are not independently verified. Do not substitute a different country's No16 sizing. Any provisional elastic law or band cross-section is a disclosed engineering assumption requiring sensitivity checks, not an OEM measurement.

parts.part: One genuine No16 natural-rubber spring loop
parts.state: Loose loop in an ordinary tray; no preinstalled invisible attachments

hardware.starting_state: Genuine assembled right-hand glove without the spring band, with printed finger hooks and holder groove exposed; electronics/camera may be installed as source background but are not manipulated. The body is counterheld at its ordinary grip or supported at the plate; neither support supplies band retention. Choose fixture orientation during preflight so gravity alone cannot imitate the claimed spring response.
hardware.tools_support: Stock YAM hands directly manipulate the soft loop and body. An ordinary open tray/nonslip mat is allowed. Do not enlarge the loop into a rigid ring or add a task-specific gripping tab.
hardware.retention: Real rubber-to-hook/groove contact and loop tension only; no snap-to, weld, magnet or proximity attachment.
hardware.known_dimensions: Named source STEP assembly has46 leaf occurrences and true source-native transforms; six relevant registered body exports and hashes are preserved. Exact finger shaft axis and a source hook support face are extracted.
hardware.unknown: Second fixed holder-hook saddle is not yet confidently assigned. Full route, hand approach, restoring direction and material response remain unverified engineering inputs.

strongest_candidates.starting_configuration: Fully assembled right-hand source glove, passive spring absent. One loose real No16 loop in tray, both arms clear. Pins, gear pair, encoder and all electronics are already installed and are not subtasks.
strongest_candidates.instruction: Fit the rubber spring loop onto the finger-base hook and the holder hook and groove, then leave the fingers opening and closing smoothly with the loop retained.
strongest_candidates.essential_skill: Acquire a narrow closed soft loop, capture its first doubled segment on a small moving-finger hook, route it in the actual fixed holder groove, then stretch and capture the opposite part on the rear hook without losing the first contact. The loop is a passive restoring spring, unlike an active driven tendon or a toothed power belt.
strongest_candidates.bimanual_challenge: One hand controls the first captured segment or counterholds the glove while the other stretches/routes the loop; regrasp must rely on the first real hook retaining it. The palm can obscure the holder even if nominal jaw aperture spans it. Direct soft-loop acquisition is a critical stock-hand question.

physical_scoring.initial: No installed spring, both real source hooks/groove accessible, actual loose loop supplied.
physical_scoring.partial: 0.25: correct moving-finger hook captures the real loop after that hand releases it.0.5: both required hooks and source groove contain the loop after both hands withdraw.0.75: one declared full safe finger open/close stroke is completed with the loop retained and no damaged hook or torn loop. Partial rungs are hierarchical and scored from external pose/contact/route inspection.
physical_scoring.full: 1.0: after released correct route and completed stroke, the loop produces the source-geometry-consistent elastic finger response under a declared small displacement/release test, with both fingers free and all hooks/groove still retaining it. Determine restoring direction from actual pivot/route geometry before fixing a reference angle. Use joint-axis-vertical orientation or an against-gravity test so a missing loop cannot earn full credit. A proposed return-angle/time threshold must be declared as a benchmark choice calibrated to the actual selected band, not attributed to Toyota.
physical_scoring.measurement: Macro photo/video of both hook contacts and groove route; protractor or camera fiducials for finger angles during the released test; visible retention after the operator/robot lets go. A real spring-force measurement may validate the declared test but no calibrated force is claimed here.
physical_scoring.invalid: Wrong finger side, bypassed groove, loop around a grip/fixture instead of the specified hook, torn band, broken hook, locked finger or band still supported by a gripper.
physical_scoring.reset: Unhook loop without damaging the printed hooks, restore finger pose and place loop loose in tray. Replace a damaged/stretched band for physical reset; do not silently re-use a failed spring.

wrong_solutions.solution: Loop only around one hook and hold the other side with a gripper
wrong_solutions.prevention: Independent release at the first rung; both hands clear at subsequent rungs; no hand contact during functional test.

wrong_solutions.solution: Stretch a shortcut across the device, bypassing the real groove
wrong_solutions.prevention: Macro route inspection at both source hook features and all groove contact sections; mere tension or proximity is not enough.

wrong_solutions.solution: Attach the loop to the wrong finger side or around the grip/bench fixture
wrong_solutions.prevention: Source-native right-glove part identity and exact hook/groove route required.

wrong_solutions.solution: Omit spring and rely on gravity or joint friction to imitate a return
wrong_solutions.prevention: Joint-axis-vertical or against-gravity displacement test; missing-band negative control must fail the functional rung.

wrong_solutions.solution: Add a hidden weld after the loop approaches a hook
wrong_solutions.prevention: Contact-only retention and a regrasp stage; the first-hook slip-off negative control must remain possible.

wrong_solutions.solution: Lock the finger at a cosmetically correct rest pose
wrong_solutions.prevention: Complete real open/close stroke and released elastic response, not a static target angle.

closest_official_tasks.head: cb29b8fc8d4ca1d6a237d91d4932115d9db7598b
closest_official_tasks.semantic_comparison: A closed toothed timing belt is already seated, and its motor mount is pulled and bolted to tension. YUBI installs a passive rubber spring onto exposed hook/groove features; there are no pulleys, teeth, translating motor mount or fastening-under-tension stage.

Do not count mere differing brands or line thickness as novelty; the opposing mechanical roles are the substantive distinction.

strongest_candidates.title: Close a real robot cycloidal reducer across two eccentric disks and a common five-roller output carrier

importance.worker: Robot hardware builder assembling the Faze4 J4 elbow reducer
importance.workflow: Designer assembly guide Elbow Assembly steps1–3, explicitly the same cycloidal construction as Joint5: phase both disks, engage the output rollers and retain the output with the real bearing cover.
importance.consequence: The joint cannot transmit its intended reduced rotation if the paired disks or shared carrier are wrong; this is directly constructing a real six-axis robot.
importance.independent_objection: This might be another gear-phasing task.
importance.resolution: Substantial overlap acknowledged; candidate includes simultaneously closing two opposed eccentric orbits around a common five-roller output and proving the completed reducer, whereas independent spur meshes and board dowels do not have this closure.

source_provenance.quote: Make shure holes on discs are alligned.
Dont overtighten the bearings , they must be able to rotate freely.
This assembly is same as one for Joint 5 cyclo .

hardware.product: Faze4 J4 elbow cycloidal reducer, using J4 filenames throughout; not mixed with the large J5 forearm
hardware.materials: Designer printed the arm in PETG; PLA is mentioned as possible if motors are not overheated. Steel commercial bearings/screws; printed disk/eccentric/carrier/case/cover.

inventory.state: Fixed to bench through an ordinary support plate; NEMA17 motor and twelve ring rollers already installed
Both carry17x23x4mm bearings; lower disk already installed per manual, second loose
Mounted on motor shaft as the source stage; opposing bearing seats create two orbital centers
Five M3x20mm screws carry ten3x8x4mm bearings with ten printed spacers; bearing pairs already assembled and free to turn
Loose with a35x47x7mm output bearing already in its seat; fiveM3x10mm screws prestarted only enough to remain in their cover bores

hardware.interfaces: Five output holes: STEP radius5.503029mm on19mm pitch radius; center-bearing recess radius11.54mm. The STEP feature origin is offset1.503029mm from its construction origin; independent STL circle extraction gives17mm eccentric seats separated about3.000mm, corresponding to1.500mm opposed eccentricity. With8mm output-bearing OD, nominal radial orbital room is1.503029mm. This clearance is part of the real cycloidal orbit, not permission to enlarge bores.
hardware.tools: Ordinary correctly sized Phillips driver for cap screws; tray; no invented alignment jig.
hardware.support: Compact genuine housing fixed in an upright bench nest, reacting to robot push/torque. Housing support is ordinary fixturing; disks and carrier remain free during assembly.
hardware.known_vs_unknown: Exact part meshes and disk analytic surfaces verified. STL installation transforms, screw lengths/cap stack, actual print friction and assembly tolerance remain engineering work. PDF contains obvious quantity typos: infer five output-screw stacks from five CAD bores and exploded picture, not its typo quantity1.

strongest_candidates.starting_state: J4 housing with genuine motor, ring rollers, eccentric and first bearing-equipped disk assembled. Second bearing-equipped disk, preassembled five-roller carrier, cover/bearing assembly and ordinary driver lie in separate trays. No belt, encoder or calibration fixture is manipulated.
strongest_candidates.instruction: Fit the second cycloidal disk and the output carrier into the J4 reducer, close and secure its bearing cover, and leave the reducer free to turn.
strongest_candidates.essential_skill: Rotate/settle the second disk on its opposite eccentric seat while respecting the fixed ring roller contacts, then acquire a common carrier through the five orbit-clearance holes of both disks. A wrong relative phase can look seated locally yet fail full input motion.
strongest_candidates.bimanual_challenge: One hand controls second-disk/carrier phase while the other stabilizes the first disk or guides the carrier; then one supports the cover against the springless loose stack while the other starts/tightens screws. Full arm, palm and tool corridor checks remain necessary;59mm disk diameter alone is not a grasp proof.

physical_scoring.initial: Lower disk installed, second and carrier absent, cap open.
physical_scoring.partial: 0.25: second disk fully supported by its actual eccentric bearing seat, inside the ring, with disk spacing within0.5mm of CAD stack and no damaged part.0.5: both disks and all five output-roller pairs engaged across both disks;0.75: real bearing cover seated, all specified cover screws retain it, robot released. Rungs are hierarchical and evaluated physically at the end.
physical_scoring.full: 1.0 only after real motor input test with hands clear: one360degree forward input and one360degree return must produce approximately32.727degrees output and return to its initial angle, with all five rollers/disk stack retained and no jamming. Proposed benchmark tolerances: output within2degrees at the end of each forward/back stage, cover gap<=0.5mm at each of four points, no detached/damaged part. These are proposed benchmark limits, not manufacturer specifications. Motor drives actual contacts; never animate output angle.
physical_scoring.measurement: Input/output witness marks and video/protractor; feeler gauge at cover; visually count retained screw heads and disk/roller stack. Small low-speed powered motor test is an ordinary bench verification, not an agent pressing an arbitrary success button. Ratio alone does not prove two disks: record a preclose macro inspection or let an external assessor open the cover after the retained motion test and count both disks, all ten output bearings, twelve ring stacks, and cover bearing. A one-disk build must fail part-count even if its ratio is correct.
physical_scoring.invalid: Any broken printed tooth/lobe, displaced ring roller, missing disk, seized bearing or stripped screw invalidates full credit. Damage must be visible/measurable, not an ungrounded hidden damage flag.
physical_scoring.reset: Remove cover, withdraw carrier and second disk, inspect bearing freedom/lobes, return first disk and eccentric to reference orientation. No consumables unless physically damaged.

wrong_solutions.solution: Seat only the upper disk; omit lower one or miss its roller holes
wrong_solutions.prevention: Count both retained disks and require every output pair engaged; full360degree ratio test jams/slips otherwise.

wrong_solutions.solution: Force carrier onto incorrectly phased disks and close the cap
wrong_solutions.prevention: Cover gap and no-damage checks plus complete forward/back motion expose a locally plausible but globally blocked assembly.

wrong_solutions.solution: Hold/turn the output by the robot during motor proof
wrong_solutions.prevention: Both hands clear by30mm and video during test; score requires motor-driven mechanical coupling.

wrong_solutions.solution: Use scripted angle/hidden latch after proximity
wrong_solutions.prevention: Forbidden implementation: output torque must pass through eccentric, disk lobes, ring rollers and output rollers; negative controls remove one essential interface.

wrong_solutions.solution: Leave cover loose but hold the stack together
wrong_solutions.prevention: External release and genuine screw retention are required; no hand-support credit.

strongest_candidates.title: Install helical wire thread inserts and clear their drive tangs from an actual robot actuator shell

importance.workflow: Shell preparation installs fourM2.5x3.75mm inserts in base and four in cover before actuator assembly.
importance.consequence: Strengthens load-bearing threaded joints of a documented research robot; no occupational aggregation required.

source_provenance.quote: Shell Base: Install four M2,5 x 3,75mm Helicoils using the installation tool. Remove the tangs using the tang break-off tool. Make sure that the tangs don't stay inside of the part.

hardware.product: Archived ODRI2dof_v1 shell; use original oldshell STL explicitly, not a newer shell without rechecking
hardware.inventory: Base33.110x37x198.499mm,28g; cover12x37x168.303mm,16g. PC-ABS FDM or Duraform HST SLS source options. Four base holes pretapped withM2.5STI tool, four Böllhoff41890250375 wire inserts. Named Hoffmann082800M2.5 tap/insertion/tang-breakoff tool set.
hardware.tools: Genuine slotted insertion mandrel, tang-breakoff punch, ordinary magnifier/tray. Do not substitute a nut, solid sleeve or invisible attachment.
hardware.state: Pretapped base supported in padded ordinary vise, no installed coil; insert loaded on tool may be legitimate focused starting stage; tang collection tray underneath accessible through-holes.
hardware.known: NominalM2.5, installed length3.75mm and exact shell body geometry verified.
hardware.unknown: ODRI does not publish free coil diameter, diamond wire section, installation-mandrel slot and tang notch dimensions. Manufacturer dimensional package must precede full coil simulation.

strongest_candidates.instruction: Install the four helical thread inserts in the actuator shell, break off and remove every drive tang, and leave all four screw bores clear.
strongest_candidates.essential_skill: Drive a contracting spring coil through an STI thread without cross-threading, stop at correct depth, then access and fracture its tang without leaving debris in the motor housing.
strongest_candidates.bimanual_challenge: Counterhold the long light shell and react driver torque, change from insertion to breakoff tool, orient shell to recover four tiny tangs.

physical_scoring.partial: 0.25 per correctly retained, straight insert at its specified depth with its tang removed and recovered; total capped0.75 until all four screw bores pass gauge.
physical_scoring.full: Four actualM2.5 gauge screws engage full intended length freely, inserts remain retained after screws withdrawn, no tang left in shell, all parts released. Depth limit must come from insert manufacturer; do not invent OEM tolerance.
physical_scoring.measurement: Macro photo/count of four inserts and recovered four tangs, gauge screw through each bore; inspect blind pockets for debris.
physical_scoring.invalid: Stripped shell thread, coil distortion, tang inside, overdeep obstructed bore; no credit from tool rotations alone.
physical_scoring.reset: New inexpensive insert and fresh shell holes for physical trials; tang breakage is consumable. Simulation restore exact fresh coils/tangs, do not pretend physical reversal.

wrong_solutions.solution: Turn a plain screw into the hole
wrong_solutions.prevention: Visible retained wire insert, gauge screw removed before scoring.

wrong_solutions.solution: Install coils but leave their tangs
wrong_solutions.prevention: Four recovered tangs and full bore gauge required.

wrong_solutions.solution: Break tang with a proximity-triggered invisible event
wrong_solutions.prevention: Actual notch fracture driven by contact/load; debris remains a body to recover.

wrong_solutions.solution: Strip receiving thread or force solid sleeve home

importance.workflow: Official motor-shaft/rotor installation: preserve brass spacer, align hub set screws to custom shaft flats, push rotor down and tighten both screws while pushing.
importance.consequence: Creates a freely rotating, axially retained robot motor assembly.

source_provenance.quote: Tighten both setscrews using a 1,5mm hex driver while pushing down on the rotor. Manually spinn the rotor to make sure that it runs freely. Pull on the rotor in the axial direction - there should be no or only minimal play.

hardware.inventory: 45mm rotor diameter,53g entire stock motor,24magnets/18slots (designer specifications); custom stainless shaft3.990mm actualCAD diameter x33.400mm length with flats; genuine brass spacer; twoM3 set screws,1.5mm hex driver; source motor stator fixed to shell by fourM3x5 flatheads.
hardware.state: Stator mounted and shaft/spacer installed per actual source; rotor loose, set screws partly in hub. This is a final assembly substep, not factory motor disassembly.
hardware.tool_support: Ordinary hexdriver held by handle, actual shell fixed in bench nest. Driver passes through rotor spoke window to radial hub screw; do not move screw to the outer rim.

strongest_candidates.title: Route and zero the actual tendon transmission of an OpenHand F3 finger

importance.workflow: Complete F3version1.0 assembly guide, lastupdatedDec15,2024; final tendon routing and5-stepzeroing procedure.
importance.consequence: Makes an underactuated robot finger respond at its calibrated rest shape instead of taking up slack or remaining preflexed; force-estimation hand depends on its real tendon route.

source_provenance.quote: The tendon is routed from the servo pulley through the tendon clearance. ... The tendons will run over the ball bearings on the dowel pins.
Unscrew the pulley until it can spin freely ... Rotate the pulley until the tendon line is taut ... Re-secure the drive pulley to the actuator

hardware.product: F3v1.0 flexure-flexure hand only; no olderT42 part substitution
hardware.inventory: TwoXM430actuators, PowerProSpectra tendon~30cm per finger, PMC780urethane flexures and DragonSkin10silicone pads, eight3mm-shaft bearings with11x4x11mm printed sleeves. Pins already installed: no dowel-joining task. Selected assembly uses actual~26.232x27.997x6mm motor pulley, M2.5x8 center screw,4-40x1/4inch distal anchor screw; a1plate159x24x122.527mm source bounds.
hardware.state: Hand frame/flexures/bearings already built; one finger tendon attached at servo per source but slack and un-routed over exposed guides; distal anchor ready. Servo held at its real zero position during zeroing stage.
hardware.tools_support: Ordinarydriver, optional ordinary fine tweezers held by stockgripper; authentic frame bench support. No expanded-scale line or rigid surrogate.
hardware.known: FullPDF and actualCAD, tendonapproxlength and guide-bearing dimensions, sourceflexure materials.
hardware.unknown: Exact chosenPowerProline gauge, finished flexure stiffness and practical line acquisition. These are material/configuration choices to declare and validate, not permission to use a rigid cable.
hardware.license: CC-BY-NC3.0 at publishedHEAD; research source inspection allowed, public benchmark reuse must preserve attribution and assess the noncommercial restriction.

strongest_candidates.instruction: Route the tendon around the finger guide bearings, secure its distal anchor, then take up slack at the zeroed motor pulley and secure the pulley so the relaxed finger opens and closes correctly.
strongest_candidates.essential_skill: Route a slack open tendon across multiple true rollers without skipping or slipping a guide, then choose tension just sufficient to remove lost motion while preserving unloaded flexure shape.
strongest_candidates.bimanual_challenge: One hand manages line tension/route while other manipulates distal anchor or pulley screw; many small regrips and finger deformations. Stockhands do not automatically acquire a submillimetreline.

physical_scoring.partial: 0.25 complete correct roller path;0.5 both real anchors retain line and slack take-up is completed;0.75 zeroed unloaded finger matches reference pose and no derailment.
physical_scoring.full: After release, a declared small realmotor pulse closes both joints through tendon force, then restoringzero returns finger to reference within3degrees perjoint, with no slipped anchor, derailment or visible slack. Proposed angles/travel must be calibrated to the actual chosen flexures, not quoted asOEMspec.
physical_scoring.measurement: Side photos atzero and actuated pose, video of guides/anchors and finger return; line tension may be checked with a light spring gauge.
physical_scoring.invalid: Torn flexure, line routed behind bearing, crushed guide, slipped anchor or finger held by gripper.
physical_scoring.reset: Loosenpulley, release distalanchor, unroute tendon and restore known slack; replacefrayed line if necessary.
